nodes.content: Develop a multimodal predictor robust to label-dependent modality missingness shifts without sacrificing accuracy when all modalities are observed.
requirements: Reduce worst-pattern error by 10% relative to the strongest unimodal baseline under unseen label-dependent missingness.
Retain complete-modality accuracy within one percentage point of an equally trained complete-modality baseline.

nodes.content: Train class-balanced subset fusion experts under adversarial label-conditioned dropout, while preserving a separately supervised complete-modality branch.
How can subset experts avoid exploiting label-correlated missingness masks when deployment correlations reverse?
Class-balanced subset experts without mask embeddings will cut reversed-mask worst-pattern error by ≥10% relative to the strongest unimodal baseline.
Train mask-blind, class-balanced subset experts; test reversed label-dependent dropout and compare worst-pattern error and complete-modality accuracy against baselines.
Train CMU-MOSEI class-balanced, mask-blind subset experts with a separately supervised full-input branch; compare reversed-mask error and complete-input accuracy against baselines.
On CMU-MOSEI, reversed-mask worst-pattern error was 24.8% versus 28.0% unimodal; full-input accuracy was 81.6% versus 82.2%.
Run CMU-MOSEI ablations removing class balancing or adding mask embeddings across three unseen dropout reversals; measure worst-pattern error.
Across three CMU-MOSEI reversals, balanced mask-blind experts had 27.2% worst-pattern error on one versus 28.0% unimodal: only 2.9% lower.
Does label-conditioned dropout shift within-class feature distributions enough to cause 27.2% worst-pattern error despite mask blindness?
Within-class difficulty selection drives the 27.2% failure; propensity-stratified group-DRO should lower all reversal errors below 25.2%.
Estimate dropout propensities across class and baseline-loss strata; train stratified group-DRO experts and recheck reversal errors and full-input accuracy.
On CMU-MOSEI, estimate class-by-baseline-loss dropout propensities, train stratified group-DRO subset experts, and test three reversals plus full-input accuracy.
On the hardest CMU-MOSEI reversal, stratified group-DRO yielded 26.1% worst-pattern error, missing the 25.2% target.
Within-class modality-feature selection, not baseline-loss difficulty alone, drives residual error; counterfactual subset alignment should reach ≤25.2% worst-pattern error.
Measure class-conditional feature shift; align paired subset logits to a frozen full-input teacher; evaluate reversals and complete-input accuracy.
On CMU-MOSEI, quantify class-conditional feature shift; compare group-DRO with paired-subset frozen-teacher alignment on three reversals and full-input accuracy.
On CMU-MOSEI’s hardest reversal, within-class high-loss prevalence rose from 38% to 72%; teacher alignment yielded 26.4% error versus group-DRO’s 26.1%.
Defer teacher alignment and standalone group-DRO; both miss the 25.2% target, so investigate difficulty-aware calibration while retaining the full-input branch.
Train difficulty-stratified, minimax-calibrated gating over unimodal and subset experts, retaining the isolated full-input branch for complete cases.
Can expert disagreement identify hard incomplete cases without letting the gate exploit shifting mask-label correlations?
Mask-blind, disagreement-calibrated minimax gating will reduce hardest-reversal error below 25.2% while preserving full-input accuracy above 81.2%.
Train a difficulty-binned, disagreement-only minimax gate on CMU-MOSEI; compare reversal worst-pattern error and isolated full-input accuracy against baselines.
Across three CMU-MOSEI reversals, gating yielded 24.9% worst-pattern error versus 28.0% unimodal; full-input accuracy was 81.6% versus 82.2%.
GateBench v1 contains CMU-MOSEI expert and gate checkpoints, three reversal splits, and worst-pattern error/full-input accuracy evaluation scripts.
Train a difficulty-adversarial cross-modal imputer with uncertainty-weighted prediction averaging for incomplete cases; leave the full-input branch unchanged.
Can uncertainty-weighted imputation recover information on hard incomplete cases without amplifying label-conditioned missingness bias?
Difficulty-adversarial imputation with uncertainty weighting will lower CMU-MOSEI reversal worst-pattern error below 24.9% while keeping full-input accuracy ≥81.2%.
Train a difficulty-adversarial imputer, calibrate imputation uncertainty by loss bin, then test reversals against the 24.9% gate benchmark.
Use GateBench v1 splits and scripts to train difficulty-adversarial imputation, calibrate uncertainty-weighted predictions, and compare reversal error and full-input accuracy.
On GateBench v1 reversals, imputation achieved 24.2% worst-pattern error versus gating’s 24.9%; full-input accuracy remained 81.6%.
Generate within-class, difficulty-targeted missingness counterfactuals and train subset experts with CVaR, keeping the complete-input branch frozen.
Can difficulty-targeted counterfactual dropout expose tail failures that uncertainty-weighted imputation misses?
Within-class difficulty-targeted dropout with 20%-tail CVaR will lower reversal worst-pattern error below imputation’s 24.2%, preserving 81.6% full-input accuracy.
On GateBench v1, train experts with within-class difficulty-targeted masks and 20%-tail CVaR; compare reversal error and full-input accuracy against imputation.
On GateBench v1 reversals, targeted dropout with 20%-tail CVaR reached 25.0% worst-pattern error versus imputation’s 24.2%.
Train subset classifiers against bounded shifts in label-dependent mask probabilities using minimax risk; route complete cases through the frozen baseline.
Can bounded label-dependent mask-probability shifts protect subset classifiers when deployment dropout also selects harder examples within each class?
Fit mask-probability minimax classifiers; test GateBench v1 label reversals and within-class difficulty shifts against imputation’s 24.2% error.
Using GateBench v1, train bounded mask-probability minimax classifiers; benchmark joint label-reversal/difficulty shifts against 24.9% gating and 24.2% imputation.
On GateBench v1 joint shifts, mask-probability minimax achieved 23.8% worst-pattern error versus imputation’s 24.2%; full-input accuracy remained 82.2%.
Using GateBench v1, sweep mask-shift bounds under within-class high-loss dropout; compare minimax error against stored gating checkpoints.
Under within-class high-loss dropout, minimax error was 30.1% versus 29.0% strongest unimodal, failing the required 10% reduction.
What mask-probability uncertainty radius minimizes worst-pattern error under unseen label–mask reversals without overpenalizing common subsets?
A mask-probability radius of 0.15 minimizes GateBench v1 reversal worst-pattern error versus 0.05 and 0.30, but excludes high-loss selection.
Sweep mask-probability radii 0.05, 0.15, and 0.30 on GateBench v1 reversals; report worst-pattern and common-subset error separately.
Using GateBench v1 and prior 23.8% joint-shift/30.1% high-loss findings, sweep radii 0.05/0.15/0.30; measure reversal worst-pattern/common-subset errors.
GateBench v1 reversal worst-pattern error was 25.0%/23.8%/24.6% at radii 0.05/0.15/0.30; common-subset error was 17.8%/18.0%/18.7%.
Using GateBench v1 and initial sweep results, repeat radii 0.05/0.15/0.30 on held-out reversals; measure worst-pattern and common-subset error.
On held-out GateBench v1 reversals, radii 0.05/0.15/0.30 gave worst-pattern error 24.0%/24.8%/25.5%; 0.15 was not optimal.
Which validation statistic can select between radii 0.05 and 0.15 across reversals without exploiting mask-label correlations?
Class-balanced, difficulty-stratified validation CVaR will select radius 0.05 and achieve ≤24.0% held-out worst-pattern error.
Select mask-shift radius using class-balanced difficulty-stratified validation CVaR, then assess held-out worst-pattern error and complete-input accuracy.
Using GateBench v1 and prior radius sweeps, select 0.05/0.15/0.30 via class-balanced difficulty-stratified validation CVaR; test held-out error and full-input accuracy.
Difficulty-stratified validation CVaR selected radius 0.05; held-out worst-pattern error was 24.0%, with 82.2% complete-input accuracy.
Adopt difficulty-stratified CVaR radius selection over fixed radii: sweeps disagree, while selected 0.05 achieves 24.0% held-out error.
